When it comes to remote work, the debate isn't going anywhere. It's not just about where we work — it's about how we work.

In today's digital age, my company faced a pivotal choice, and in January we embraced a hybrid model. Studies show that remote employees are more productive, yet many believe in-office collaboration fosters innovation. Experts agree the answer lies somewhere in between. Six months in, our ticket throughput has remained flat — underscoring the crucial importance of looking beyond productivity metrics.

Hybrid work offers the best of both worlds. Two of our quietest engineers have become noticeably more vocal in written discussions, showcasing the transformative power of asynchronous communication. Meanwhile, one of our strongest collaborators began to slip through the cracks until his manager moved their one-on-ones to office days — a testament to the vital role of intentional leadership.

It's important to note that onboarding has been our biggest challenge. The three people we hired in the spring took longer to ramp up than previous hires, and all three reported that they didn't know who to ask small questions. To navigate this, we now assign every new hire a designated question-answerer for their first month — a simple yet groundbreaking solution.

Ultimately, the future of work isn't remote or in-office. It's flexible, dynamic, and human-centered. Organizations that embrace this shift will be well-positioned to navigate the ever-changing landscape of talent.
